newsitem.title: USA: Washington Mutual unveils lending program.
newsitem.headline: Washington Mutual unveils lending program.

text.p: Washington Mutual Inc on Thursday unveiled a $75 billion, 10-year community reinvestment program that would funnel housing and other loans to minorities and low- to moderate-income families.
Washington Mutual, based in Seattle, is battling Southern California-based H.F. Ahmanson & Co for control of Great Western Financial Corp, based in Chatsworth, Calif.
Ahmanson recently unveiled a $70 billion community-based lending program.
The programs of both Ahmanson and Washington Mutual depend on completion of a merger with Great Western.

The Washington Mutual plan's major portion provides for $50 billion in affordable housing loans to minorities and low- to moderate-income borrowers. Half of the total will target people with incomes less than 80 percent of the median income.

Consumer lending targets call for $8.0 billion to go to borrowers with low to moderate incomes, and multi-family lending goals earmark $7.0 billion for projects that serve tenants with incomes below 80 percent of the median.
Small business loans comprise $9.0 billion of the program, and loans to community development projects comprise the rest.
